cards.explanation: The answer is “I am a god.” God says the ruler's heart is proud, and he has said, “…‘I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods in the heart of the sea.’…” That's a LOT to claim when you're standing in a city by the water. God answers with one plain line right after it.

The answer is True. God says the ruler is a man and not a god. His words are, “Yet you are a man and not a god, though you have regarded your heart as that of a god.” One sentence, and the whole claim is answered. A man can sit in a fancy seat all day and still be a man.

The answer is by his wisdom and understanding. God says, “By your wisdom and understanding you have gained your wealth and amassed gold and silver for your treasuries.” Then the next verse adds his great skill in trading. The wealth is real, friends, and so is the pride that came with it.

The answer is the most ruthless of nations. God says, “…I will bring foreigners against you, the most ruthless of nations.” That's not a gentle description. When God names who is coming, He picks a hard word.

The answer is False. God says these foreigners “…will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and will defile your splendor.” That's the opposite of treating it with respect. The ruler's splendor won't be handled gently.
The answer is that He has spoken. God closes with, “For I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.” No more arguing and no extra evidence needed. When He has spoken, that's the last word on it.
The answer is True. The lament opens, “You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.” Notice the "were." It starts by looking back at what the king of Tyre was.

The answer is every kind of precious stone. God says, “Every kind of precious stone adorned you: ruby, topaz, and diamond, beryl, onyx, and jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald.” Then He adds gold for the mountings and settings. It's a long list, friends, and the lament reads every bit of it.
The answer is a guardian cherub. God says, “You were anointed as a guardian cherub, for I had ordained you.” That's the title He gives the king of Tyre. It's one more thing the lament says he was.
The answer is False. God says, “From the day you were created you were blameless in your ways…” Blameless came first. The wickedness was found in him later.

The answer is that God drove him from the mountain of God. God says, “So I drove you in disgrace from the mountain of God, and I banished you, O guardian cherub, from among the fiery stones.” It's a heavy moment, and the lament tells it plainly. The sin came first, and then he was driven out.

The answer is to the earth. God says the king's heart grew proud of his beauty, and then, “so I cast you to the earth; I made you a spectacle before kings.” The casting down follows right after the pride. After that, he's made a spectacle before kings.

The answer is sanctuaries. God says, “…you have profaned your sanctuaries.” He ties it to the multitude of the king's iniquities and the dishonesty of his trading. Two things pile up on that one sentence.
The answer is True. God says, “So I made fire come from within you, and it consumed you.” The fire came from inside him. It's a hard line, friends, and the lament doesn't soften it.
The answer is that they are appalled over him. God says, “All the nations who know you are appalled over you.” Appalled is a strong word. That's how the nations who know him respond to his end.

The answer is that He will be glorified within her. God says, “Behold, I am against you, O Sidon, and I will be glorified within you.” He doesn't say He'll build her up. He says He will be glorified there.

The answer is True. God says, “They will know that I am the LORD when I execute judgments against her and demonstrate My holiness through her.” It's a heavy word for Sidon. The verse says they will know exactly who He is.

The answer is a pricking brier or a painful thorn. God says Israel “…will no longer face a pricking brier or a painful thorn from all around them who treat them with contempt.” It's a plant that stings. You know that feeling if you've ever grabbed the wrong branch.

The answer is that He will show Himself holy among them. God says, “…I will show Myself holy among them in the sight of the nations.” The nations get a front-row seat, friends. It's about who He is in the middle of His people.
The answer is land. God says, “Then they will dwell in their own land, which I have given to My servant Jacob.” The land is described as already given. God says they will dwell there.

The answer is False. God says, “They will dwell securely when I execute judgments against all those around them who treat them with contempt.” God Himself executes the judgments. Israel's armies aren't mentioned.
